policy: Exact individual membership and reviewed component scope; fill unavailable values only, preserve earlier reviews. Published model and calibration estimates retain their status. No system-total or subsystem-total masses, blended flux, minimum masses, assumed abundance, or fabricated component velocities.

bright-dschubba.note: Dschubba A: primary-only diskless SED/rotating-star model from Suffak et al. (2020), Table 4. Model uncertainties do not include inclination, distance or reddening systematics. Scalar radius is the Stefan-Boltzmann equivalent from the adopted luminosity and effective temperature; published polar/equatorial radii are 6.4/6.8 solar radii. Existing shared catalog distance is retained; no parent photometry or velocities restored.

spectral_type.caveat: Adopted early-B main-sequence classification; subtype is a range, not a measured precise subtype.

orb6-16003-2237-a-b-b.note: Dschubba B: 8.2 +/- 0.6 solar masses from the evolutionary/orbit model of Miroshnichenko et al. (2013), Section 3.4. The adopted B1-B3 main-sequence classification and 20000-24000 K range remain ranges; no precise scalar temperature, bolometric luminosity, radius, abundance or individual velocity inferred.

spectral_type.caveat: Published common classification of the Be primary; B4IV and B6V have also been reported. Rapid rotation and gravity darkening make its apparent classification aspect-dependent.

bright-achernar.note: Achernar: individual component constraints from Kervella et al. (2022). A mass subtracts the model-based B mass from the dynamical total; B mass is evolutionary-model based. Radii/temperatures/luminosities use component SEDs and mean limb-darkened diameters. A age is a rotating evolutionary-track estimate; no B age copied from A. A remains a fast rotator, so the scalar diameter/temperature are averages.

orb6-01377-5714-a-b-b.note: Achernar: individual component constraints from Kervella et al. (2022). A mass subtracts the model-based B mass from the dynamical total; B mass is evolutionary-model based. Radii/temperatures/luminosities use component SEDs and mean limb-darkened diameters. A age is a rotating evolutionary-track estimate; no B age copied from A. A remains a fast rotator, so the scalar diameter/temperature are averages.

bright-rasalhague.note: Rasalhague: individual dynamical masses from Gardner et al. (2021), Table 4. A surface-averaged effective temperature/luminosity and model age are from Zhao et al. (2009), as compiled in that table. Its radius is the Stefan-Boltzmann equivalent, not a polar/equatorial radius. Secondary J/K photometry is not Johnson V or bolometric luminosity; solar composition assumed in evolution models is not a measured abundance.

orb6-17349+1234-a-b-b.note: Rasalhague: individual dynamical masses from Gardner et al. (2021), Table 4. A surface-averaged effective temperature/luminosity and model age are from Zhao et al. hip-102281.note: Delta Delphini: separate dynamical masses and interferometric/SED stellar properties from Gardner et al. (2018), Tables 6 and 11. R/H magnitudes are not adopted as Johnson V. No common age imposed: the paper finds an evolutionary age discrepancy between components.

orb6-20435+1504-a-b-b.note: Delta Delphini: separate dynamical masses and interferometric/SED stellar properties from Gardner et al. (2018), Tables 6 and 11. R/H magnitudes are not adopted as Johnson V. No common age imposed: the paper finds an evolutionary age discrepancy between components.

hip-68756.note: Thuban: individual masses/radii/temperatures from Pavlovski et al. (2022), Table 6. Luminosities are exponentiated published log L (2.380 for A, 1.677 for B; the original paper takes precedence over DEBCat rounding/transcription). Ages are separately fitted model ages; their mismatch is retained, not forced to a shared age. System abundance and total light remain unassigned to individual components.

orb6-14044+6423-a-b-b.note: Thuban: individual masses/radii/temperatures from Pavlovski et al. (2022), Table 6. apparent_mag.caveat: Published decomposition of Johnson V using resolved brightness differences, not ORB6 band-ambiguous magnitudes.
